title: GraphLoRA: Structure-Aware Contrastive Low-Rank Adaptation for Cross-Graph Transfer Learning

problem.claim: Adapting a well-trained GNN to new graphs with varying feature and structural distributions is challenging.

gap.claim: Existing GNN transfer-learning research overlooks distribution discrepancies across graph datasets, especially across different distributions.

contributions.claim: GraphLoRA is a parameter-efficient method for transferring well-trained GNNs across diverse graph domains.
Structure-aware Maximum Mean Discrepancy aligns divergent node-feature distributions between source and target graphs.

A small trainable GNN is injected alongside the pre-trained GNN to bridge structural distribution gaps and mitigate catastrophic forgetting, with structure-aware regularization for scarce target labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight real-world datasets reportedly show GraphLoRA outperforming fourteen baselines while tuning 20% of parameters, including across disparate graph domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs perform graph analytical tasks across domains.
GNN transferability is limited, particularly across differing graph distributions.
The authors propose GraphLoRA for parameter-efficient cross-domain GNN transfer.
GraphLoRA aligns feature distributions, adapts structural representations with a low-rank trainable GNN, and regularizes adaptation under scarce labels.
The authors report experiments across eight datasets against fourteen baselines with 20% parameter tuning.

source_observation.claim: Cross-graph transfer may require addressing both node-feature and structural distribution gaps.

interpretation.claim: Transfer methods should align multiple distributional aspects rather than treating domain shift as a single discrepancy.

application.claim: For another graph-transfer setting, separately assess feature alignment and structural adaptation while limiting trainable parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported graph domains or label regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the eight datasets, task definitions, baseline identities, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, ablations, or details of the adaptation architecture and regularization objective.
